title: Number of Ways of Cutting a Pizza
summary: Given a rectangular pizza with 'A' for apples and '.' for empty cells, and an integer k, determine the number of ways to cut the pizza into k pieces, ensuring each piece has at least one apple.
statement: Given a rectangular pizza with 'A' for apples and '.' for empty cells, and an integer k, determine the number of ways to cut the pizza into k pieces, ensuring each piece has at least one apple. Each cut is either vertical or horizontal, and the last piece goes to the last person. Return the count modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Make k-1 horizontal or vertical cuts, always giving away the upper or left piece.
Every final piece needs at least one apple; return ways modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Precompute apple counts for every bottom-right suffix.
State is the remaining suffix top-left coordinate and number of pieces still required.
Try each horizontal or vertical cut whose removed top/left piece has an apple.
The final suffix must contain an apple; every ordered cut sequence has a unique first cut.
editorial: The final suffix must contain an apple; every ordered cut sequence has a unique first cut.

tests.explanation: Three ordered cut sequences produce three apple-containing pieces.
Only one sequence distributes the three apples among three pieces.
